title: Al-Muqtadir, the All-Powerful
tomorrow: the thing you keep pushing to tomorrow: is there a Name for that?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Qadir, the Able, and two ways of knocking on the same door. The line: able. Today the word gets longer, and so does the power.

In the fall, sidewalks crunch. Step on one dry leaf and you hear the end of a whole summer: it was green, it drank the rain, and now it's paper and dust under your shoe. The Qur'an has a verse that is exactly that sound. A whole season, rain to crackle, in one sentence. And it doesn't end on the leaf. It ends on today's Name.
screen: `THE CRUNCH UNDER YOUR SHOE.` → `A SEASON IN ONE SENTENCE.` → `IT ENDS ON THE NAME.`

segments.voice: It's in surah al-Kahf. God tells the Prophet to give people a picture of this world's life. Water comes down from the sky. The plants of the earth drink it and mingle, and everything goes green. Then it becomes dry stalks, and the wind scatters them. And the verse closes: Allah has power over all things. The Arabic word there is muqtadir, and today's Name is Al-Muqtadir, the All-Powerful. Yesterday's Name, Al-Qadir, comes from the same family of letters. Some scholars hear the longer form as stronger: not only able, but power actually used, deciding how every season turns. Now hold the verse up like the leaf. It's humbling: the green doesn't stay, not the summer, not the streak, not the season of your life that felt like it would last. And it's steadying: the One with power over the drying is the same One over the rain. The very next verse says what does last. Wealth and children, it says, are the shine of this world's life, but the good deeds that remain are better with your Lord. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in this picture, nothing about the leaf is wasted. It just isn't the part that lasts.
screen: `RAIN, GREEN, DRY STALKS, WIND.` · `MUQTADIR: POWER OVER ALL THINGS.` · `HUMBLING, AND STEADYING.` · `GOOD DEEDS ARE WHAT REMAIN.` · then, large: `ALL POWER.`

segments.voice: Find something from a plant near you: a dry leaf, a sprig of herb, a flower going brown, even the leaves in a tea bag. Hold it in your open palm for the sit, feel how light it is now, and close your hand gently once to hear it. Let it say both things: the green passes, and all power stays with the One who sends the rain.
screen: `SOMETHING FROM A PLANT.` · `HOLD IT. HEAR IT.` · `THE GREEN PASSES.`

segments.voice: Al-Muqtadir. The All-Powerful, determining all: the word that closes the verse of the rain and the wind.
Hold on to this: all power, over the green and the dry alike. Name seventy, and the leaves keep falling.

howItsDone: Reciting surah al-Kahf on Fridays is a custom rooted in hadith; its parable of the rain and the scattered stalks is verse 45, and Muslims call on Allah by His Names in personal du'a.

myth: Al-Muqtadir and Al-Qadir are one Name said twice
they're two Names. some scholars hear Al-Muqtadir as power fully used, deciding all.
the parable in al-Kahf runs from rain to dry stalks the wind scatters
a whole season in one verse, closing on Allah's power over all things.
the parable says green and growing things are worthless

fork.setup: your aunt's garden dies in a heat wave. she sighs, 'what's even the point of planting?' what does the verse of the rain and the wind give her?
options: the green never lasts, but the One with power over the drying sends the rain too.
plant tougher things next time; with enough effort nothing has to die.
the dying is a sign she did something wrong this year.
fork.reveal: the verse holds rain and wind together and closes on the One with power over both. the next verse names what lasts: good deeds.

original.note: Arabic: the All-Powerful. the verse of the rain and the wind (18:45) ends with muqtadir.

chat.says: portal opens tomorrow. i've refreshed my email all night like it'll open early. how do i stop??
options: Put the phone down and hold something real. The One with all power holds tomorrow too.
Keep checking. Trusting His power means being ready the second the news drops.
Decide now it's a no, so whatever comes tomorrow can't hurt you as much.
chat.meaning: Al-Muqtadir has power over all things, the rain and the drying alike. Trust can be physical: put the screen down and hold on.
